issues.legal_issue: A compulsory auction of business assets to recover a statutory debt can constitute a sale for purposes of taxing the excess over the assets’ written-down value.
material_facts: A statutory levy arose from an activity the assessee had voluntarily undertaken.
The assessee knew that the activity was subject to the levy and that unpaid amounts could be recovered as land revenue through an auction of its property.
The assessee’s business assets were auctioned to recover the unpaid levy, and the tax assessment included the excess of the sale proceeds over the assets’ written-down value.
issues.conclusion: The auction sale fell within the meaning of “sold” in section 10(2)(vii) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, despite being conducted to recover the debt.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(2)(vii) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, a sale need not be wholly voluntary where the taxpayer voluntarily undertook the activity giving rise to the liability and thereby accepted the statutory framework, including recovery by auction on default. The Court considered Calcutta Electric Supply Corporation Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, West Bengal, which treated sale as ordinarily requiring voluntary agreement; Indian Steel & Wire Products Ltd. v. State of Madras, which held that a transaction can be a sale where mutual assent is not altogether excluded; and R.B. Lachman Das Mohanlal & Sons v. Commissioner of Income-tax, U.P., which it found not truly apposite.

predicates.business_asset_disposal_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns the tax treatment of the disposal of assets used in a business.
predicates.statutory_debt_recovery_auction: A public authority auctioned the taxpayer’s property to recover a debt under a statutory recovery process.
predicates.taxpayer_voluntarily_undertook_activity_: The taxpayer voluntarily engaged in an activity that gave rise to the debt being recovered.
predicates.taxpayer_knew_default_exposed_assets_to_: The taxpayer knew that failing to pay the debt could lead to its property being sold at auction.

issues.definition: When a business-asset tax assessment concerns an auction to recover a statutory debt arising from an activity the taxpayer voluntarily undertook, and the taxpayer knew default could expose its assets to auction, the disposal is treated as a sale for business-tax purposes.

issues.legal_issue: In a statutory recovery auction where the prescribed certificate effects the transfer of property, the sale takes place when the certificate is issued rather than when the auction is held.
material_facts: The taxpayer’s property was auctioned to recover unpaid statutory dues, and the purchaser paid the full purchase price shortly after the auction.
Objections delayed the issue of the sale certificate until after the auction and payment.
The applicable recovery procedure provided for confirmation of the sale and made the certificate a valid transfer of the property.
The taxpayer relied on the general civil-procedure rule that can deem a purchaser’s title to relate back to the auction, but the recovery procedure was inconsistent with applying that rule.
issues.conclusion: The sale took place when the certificate was issued, because the certificate itself effected the transfer and the recovery procedure excluded the general relation-back rule. Accordingly, the sale was not treated as having occurred before the capital-gains provision became effective.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 279 and 286 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, and rule 281 of the Rules provide for recovery and auction of property, while rule 285-M makes the certificate a valid transfer. Section 341 applies the Code of Civil Procedure only insofar as it is consistent with the Act; therefore section 65 of the Code does not apply where it would conflict with the certificate-based transfer procedure. The sale date consequently determines whether section 12B of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, applies.

rule.if: tax_timing_dispute_over_recovery_sale and recovery_auction_proceeding and certificate_effects_transfer and recovery_process_displaces_general_relation_back_rule

predicates.tax_timing_dispute_over_recovery_sale: The proceeding concerns when a property sale in a recovery process occurred for tax purposes.
predicates.recovery_auction_proceeding: A public authority auctioned property to recover a debt through a prescribed recovery process.
predicates.certificate_effects_transfer: The prescribed process made the sale certificate the instrument that transferred ownership to the purchaser.
predicates.recovery_process_displaces_general_relat: The recovery process did not permit the general procedural rule that would date the transfer back to the auction.

issues.definition: When a tax-timing dispute concerns a recovery auction and the applicable process makes the certificate the instrument of transfer while displacing a general relation-back rule, the sale is treated as occurring when the certificate is issued.
